newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel may vote May 7 on new telecoms bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel may vote May 7 on new telecoms bill.

text.p: A final draft of Brazil's new General Telecommunications Law is slated to be read May 5 to its Chamber of Deputies panel and may be voted on two days later, a congressional official said.
A spokeswoman for Deputy Alberto Goldman, who is in change of preparing the bill in its special lower house committee, said the lawmaker will complete his final draft on Wednesday.
The law will lay down the rules for the privatization of federal telecommunications system Telebras, create a new sector watchdog and establish the rules for telecoms operators in Brazil.
The spokeswoman said a preliminary draft of the bill contains some modifications to the version presented to Congress by the government last December.

For instance, the rough version would not restrict foreign capital participation in privatizations but would give the president the right to set a limit deemed necessary as a result of local or international economic and political circumstances.
It also would set a five-year limit on operating licenses issued by the new regulatory body and determine where licensing fees would be deposited, she said.
"That's a controversial item," the spokeswoman said.
If approved in the 30-member panel by at least 16 votes, the bill would then go to the full Chamber and, afterward, to the Senate, she said.
She added that lower house approval could well come next month, possibly within days of the committee vote
The government hopes to privatize Telebras starting late this year or early in 1998, beginning with its two largest units Telesp and Embratel.
